item.title: Supreme Court Hears Arguments in President’s Attempt to Fire Fed Reserve Member
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Supreme Court Justices from across the spectrum seemed skeptical about the President’s efforts to remove one of the Federal Reserve Board members. The President has accused Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud and is looking to fire her. Experts have said it's an unprecedented case and a test of the President’s power to remove people at independent agencies.

item.title: Washington Weighs Crackdown on Credit Card Interest and Late Fees as Consumer Costs Climb
item.description: From grocery bills to rent payments, Americans say every dollar matters — and now, there’s growing momentum to rein in what critics call predatory credit card fees.

item.title: House Passes Homeland Security Funding even with Democrats Opposition over ICE
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - In a 220 to 207 vote, the House passed a bill to fund the Department of Homeland Security. The bill received a lot of scrutiny from Democrats as they tried to reign in funding for ICE.

item.title: Democrat Congresswoman Questions Administrations Reasons to Acquire Greenland
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - President Donald Trump announced the US and NATO have agreed to a framework regarding Greenland but details have been limited as to what that framework looks like. The US already has a military presence on the Danish territory. So, a Congressional Democratic Delegate is questioning why the administration wants to take control of the island.

item.title: Langworthy, Oversight Committee Advance Contempt Proceedings Against Clintons in Epstein Investigation
item.description: Lawmakers in Washington have advanced contempt proceedings against Bill and Hillary Clinton, accusing them of stonewalling a federal investigation tied to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Senate Democrats Threaten to Block DHS Funding Over Minneapolis ICE Shootings
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Senate Democrats are now threatening to block funding for the Homeland Security Department after federal agents shot and killed a Minneapolis resident over the weekend. Blocking funding could potentially trigger another government shutdown.

item.title: Democrats Urge DHS Secretary to Resign, Pursuing Impeachment Proceedings
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Following weeks of intense scrutiny of ICE operations, Democrats are looking to pursue impeachment charges against Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem following the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis.

item.title: How a Partial Government Shutdown Over DHS Funding Could Compare to Last Shutdown
item.description: Washington is gearing up for another funding fight — and this one could shut down part of the federal government. At the center of it all: the Department of Homeland Security and growing backlash over immigration enforcement.

item.title: Secretary Rubio Testifies to Senate Committee on Venezuela
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations committee taking questions from Senators for the first time publicly since US forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

item.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Tensions Escalate After Trump Threatens Tariffs Over China Partnership
item.description: President Trump is once again threatening an escalation in trade tensions with Canada. The warning is tied to a new potential relationship between Canada and one of America’s greatest adversaries.
